nuggets.title: Compromised Pod Uses Over-Broad IAM Role to Dump Secrets

scenario.symptoms: Security detects an unknown process listing every secret path under /prod/* from a compromised microservice pod. Cloud audit logs show 40,000 Secret Manager read API calls in 10 minutes.
scenario.interviewerSetup: All production pods share one generic IAM role with secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on resource * . Workload identity is enabled but not scoped per service or secret.

incident.headline: Shared IAM credentials let any compromised workload read every production secret

agenda.goal: Bind secret access to workload identity with least-privilege policies per service and environment.
agenda.opener: An attacker inside one pod started pulling secrets for unrelated services. How should identity and authorization work when a service fetches its credentials?

evidence.strong: Per-service workload identity (SPIFFE/K8s SA/JWT), ABAC or policy mapping service identity to explicit secret ARNs, separate roles per env, deny-by-default, short-lived tokens, and break-glass roles audited separately.
evidence.adequate: Separate IAM roles per service but still coarse resource wildcards.
evidence.weak: Long-lived static API keys baked into images or one shared cluster role.

misconceptions.pattern: Assumes network policies alone prevent lateral secret theft.
misconceptions.challenge: If the attacker already runs code in the cluster, what stops them from calling the secrets API with the pod's credentials?

probes: How does a new microservice get permission to read only its DB password?
What breaks if every pod shares one role?
hints: Map identity to the running binary, not the whole cluster.
Least privilege means listing explicit secret names.
agenda.referenceFix: Workload identity per service with policy that grants GetSecret only on named paths; no wildcard prod/*; audit all access.

nuggets.title: Database Credential Rotation Triggers Fleet-Wide Restart Storm

scenario.symptoms: During scheduled DB password rotation, 800 services restart simultaneously and checkout API error rate hits 40% for 12 minutes. Connection pools hold stale passwords until process restart.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Rotation updates the secret in the vault but apps only reload credentials on startup. Orchestration detects failed health checks and replaces all pods at once.

incident.headline: Apps lack hot reload of rotated credentials, forcing correlated restarts across the fleet

agenda.goal: Rotate secrets without downtime using versioned secrets, gradual reload, and dual-credential overlap windows.
agenda.opener: Our nightly DB password rotation took down checkout. How should services pick up a new database password without a full restart?

evidence.strong: Dual-active secret versions during overlap, sidecar or SDK push/subscribe on rotation events, connection pool drain and refresh, staged rollout per AZ, automated validation before revoking old version.
evidence.adequate: Rolling restart triggered by config change but no overlap window.
evidence.weak: Manual SSH to update env files then restart everything.

misconceptions.pattern: Believes atomic swap of one password works if all apps restart together.
misconceptions.challenge: What happens to in-flight transactions during a simultaneous fleet restart?

probes: How long can two DB passwords remain valid?
Who notifies running processes that the secret version changed?
hints: Think push notification vs poll on boot only.
Drain connections before revoking the old secret.
agenda.referenceFix: Versioned secrets with overlap, hot reload via agent webhook/SIGHUP, pool refresh, canary reload before fleet-wide revoke.

nuggets.title: Long-Lived Sidecar Cache Serves Revoked API Keys

scenario.symptoms: After revoking a leaked partner API key, traffic with the old key continues for 45 minutes. Incident response cannot confirm full containment.
scenario.interviewerSetup: The secrets sidecar caches fetched secrets in memory for 60 minutes to reduce vault QPS. Revocation updates the vault but not in-process caches.

incident.headline: Aggressive local caching delays propagation of secret revocation across running instances

agenda.goal: Cache secrets safely with bounded TTL, version checks, and push invalidation on revoke or rotation.
agenda.opener: We revoked a leaked key but partners could still authenticate for nearly an hour. How does caching interact with revocation?

evidence.strong: Short TTL plus version metadata, subscribe to rotation/revoke events, negative cache avoided for auth secrets, encrypt cache at rest in sidecar, fallback to live vault on version mismatch.
evidence.adequate: TTL under 5 minutes without push invalidation.
evidence.weak: Infinite in-memory cache to save vault costs.

misconceptions.pattern: Assumes deleting a secret in the vault instantly stops all usage.
misconceptions.challenge: How many running sidecars still hold the old value in RAM?

probes: What event should flush a cached secret?
How do you balance vault QPS vs security?
hints: Revocation is an signal, not only a storage delete.
Version numbers help detect stale cache.
agenda.referenceFix: Short TTL, vault revision in cache key, pub/sub invalidation on revoke, force refresh hook for incident response.

nuggets.title: Emergency Revoke Takes 20 Minutes to Reach Edge Nodes

scenario.symptoms: A signing key for JWT issuance is compromised. Security triggers global revoke, but edge POPs continue minting valid tokens with the old key for 20 minutes.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Revocation is written to the central vault; regional agents poll every 15 minutes. JWT validators cache JWKS for 24 hours without forced refresh.

incident.headline: Poll-based revocation and long JWKS TTL extend exposure after key compromise

agenda.goal: Propagate revocations in seconds with push fanout, short-lived tokens, and JWKS refresh on incident.
agenda.opener: We revoked a signing key but attackers could still get valid JWTs at the edge. How fast must revocation reach every validator?

evidence.strong: Push revocation events to all agents, break-glass JWKS flush, short JWT lifetimes with refresh, key version in token header, centralized revoke list checked at auth gateway.
evidence.adequate: Poll every 60s without JWKS cache bust.
evidence.weak: Only delete key in vault and hope for the best.

misconceptions.pattern: Treats revocation as deleting a row in one database.
misconceptions.challenge: Who tells thousands of edge caches to forget the old public key?

probes: What is the maximum acceptable time for a revoked key to stop working?
How do validators learn about a new key version?
hints: Push beats slow poll for incidents.
agenda.referenceFix: Real-time revoke bus, forced JWKS reload, token lifetimes under 15m, optional denylist at gateway during incident.

nuggets.title: Forensics Blocked by Missing Secret Access Audit Trail

scenario.symptoms: Compliance audit flags inability to prove who read production TLS private keys during a suspected insider incident. Vault metrics show read volume but not caller identity tied to workloads.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Applications fetch secrets via a shared sidecar without propagating service identity in audit logs. Logs aggregate at the node level only.

incident.headline: Secret access auditing cannot attribute reads to specific workloads or users

agenda.goal: Emit immutable audit events with workload identity, secret name, version, and purpose for every access.
agenda.opener: Auditors need to know which service read a production TLS key last Tuesday. What does your audit trail capture today?

evidence.strong: Structured audit to SIEM with SPIFFE ID, K8s namespace/pod, secret ARN, version, justification tag, hash chain or WORM storage, alerts on anomalous volume.
evidence.adequate: Vault native audit enabled but without workload context.
evidence.weak: No audit logging on secret reads.

misconceptions.pattern: Believes aggregate read metrics satisfy compliance.
misconceptions.challenge: Can you name the exact workload that exported a private key?

probes: What fields must each audit record contain?
How do you detect bulk exfiltration early?
hints: Identity must flow from app through sidecar to vault.
agenda.referenceFix: Per-request audit with service identity, dual shipping to SIEM, anomaly detection on secret path patterns.
